title: The Closed-Book Test: Why Models Hallucinate
text: Hi, I'm Rishika. Imagine a test with the book closed. You're guessing from memory. Now imagine it open book. You flip to the right page before you answer. That's retrieval augmented generation. text: Training data is frozen at some pass date. Ask about anything outside that book and it doesn't say, "I don't know." It guesses confidently. That's a hallucination. Here's the fix. title: Under the Hood: Vector Embeddings and Nearest Neighbors
text: And the system grabs the nearest ones. Those pages get handed to the model as context and it answers from that, not from memory. Why this is worth it? With RA, answers are grounded in real checkable pages, not memory. Hallucinations drop because the model is reading, not guessing. And when your knowledge changes, you swap a page, not the model. title: The Real Benefits: Grounded Answers & No Retraining
text: Limit. RAG is only as good as the book it's handed. Feed it a bad or incomplete book, and it hands back a bad answer, dressed up as if it were grounded. RAG doesn't make the model smarter. It makes it better informed.
